extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and third-party requesters preparing or responding to ex parte reexamination requests before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary requirements and best practices for preparing, filing, and processing ex parte reexamination requests and related reexamination prosecution documents before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of cited reference in request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester’s response to the notice explicitly withdraws the Jones patent from the request, then no explanation is required as to the Jones reference, and all combinations advanced in the request that contained Jones are deemed to be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a cited reference is explicitly withdrawn in response to an Office notice, the Office will treat that reference and any combinations relying on it as withdrawn; no further explanation as to that reference is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance despite non-compliance if explanation is clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the request fails to comply with one of the above-identified requirements, the request may be accepted if it is readily understood from the explanation provided in the request as to how the cited patents or printed publications are applied to all claims which requester considers to merit reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-compliant request can still be granted a filing date if the submitted explanation clearly shows how the cited art applies to the claims at issue; this is a limited exception and depends on whether the explanation makes the application of the cited art readily understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits/declarations/other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications in more detail may be considered in reexamination. See MPEP § 2258.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting affidavits/declarations can be submitted to explain or clarify prior art documents or dates; consult MPEP § 2258 for handling during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of admissions as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission, per se, may not be the basis for establishing a substantial new question of patentability; however, an admission by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions by the patent owner can be used with patents/printed publications to determine scope/content of prior art in a rejection, but an admission alone is generally insufficient to establish an SNQ. Admissions must stand on their own and may not be supplemented by additional information. Third parties may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the patent file or court record unless those admissions are entered into a court record and filed as a court document (which still may not be given weight as an admission for establishing SNQ). See MPEP § 2258 for examination-stage handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of each relied-on prior art document (legibility & translations)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is required that a copy of each patent or printed publication relied on or referred to in the request be filed with the request (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3)). If the copy provided is not legible, or is such that its image scanned into the Image File Wrapper system (IFW) will not be legible, it is deemed to not have been provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legible copies; illegible copies are treated as not provided and trigger a Notice of Failure to Comply. Photographs/color submissions that are legible will be retained in an 'artifact' file. Non-English documents require an English translation of all necessary and pertinent parts (an abstract or summary is usually not sufficient). The Office may not consider untranslated matter beyond what is submitted in translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include prior art from earlier prosecution (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is helpful to include copies of the prior art considered (via a 37 CFR 1.555 information disclosure statement) during earlier prosecution of the patent for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting both prior IDS-cited art and new art allows comparison to determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is present. See MPEP § 2242.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions/waiver for U.S. patent copies and prohibited submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the requirement for a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to in the request, this requirement is not currently being enforced to require copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent publications; and the requirement is deemed waived to that extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (these may be mistaken for new filings); instead provide the application/proceeding number and status. Submissions not permitted entry will be returned, expunged, or discarded at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters are required under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) to include a copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested, to serve as the specification for the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full printed copy (double column format including front page) so the abstract, drawings, specification, and claims are present. Include copies of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or prior reexamination certificate, and any relevant Federal Court decisions, complaints, or interference decisions so a complete patent history is before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service when requester is not patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is a person other than the patent owner, the owner of the patent must be served with a copy of the request in its entirety. The certificate of service must set forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service, be attached to the request, and a copy of the certificate of service must be included in the copy served on the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after reasonable effort, supply a duplicate copy to the Office with a cover letter explaining the efforts made. To avoid duplicate-fee errors, callers are encouraged to clearly label cover letters (example wording provided). See MPEP § 2266.03 regarding service details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner may include proposed amendments with request
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.510(e), a patent owner may include a proposed amendment with his or her request. Any such amendment must be in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530(d) through (j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to add claims may incur excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4). The decision on whether to grant the reexamination request is made based on the claims in effect at the time of the request (i.e., proposed amendments do not affect the initial decision), though subsequent prosecution proceeds on the basis of amended claims if the request is granted. See MPEP § 2250 for format and requirements and §§ 2234 and 2250 for related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address controls official communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner or owners in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the correspondence address for the patent (37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and papers filed on behalf of a patent owner must be signed by the patent owner(s) or by an attorney/agent of record, or by a registered attorney or agent acting under 37 CFR 1.34. Double correspondence with both owner and owner’s attorney/agent normally will not be undertaken. If the patent owner desires a different attorney/agent to receive correspondence, a new power of attorney must be filed (see MPEP § 324). Provide the Mail Stop information prominently on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney/agent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw from a patent and/or a reexamination proceeding, the practitioner(s) must certify that they: (1) gave reasonable notice to the client prior to the expiration of the response period that they intend to withdraw; (2) delivered to the client all papers and property to which the client is entitled; and (3) notified the client of any responses that may be due and the time frame to respond (37 CFR 11.116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office no longer requires 30 days remaining in any response period as a precondition. 'Reasonable notice' should allow the client time to retain new counsel. The practitioner’s responsibility to notify a former client is not eliminated by withdrawing as attorney/agent of record. See MPEP § 402.06 for sample forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing and delivery instructions for filings and hand-carried correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests and subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence mailed via USPS should be addressed to Mail Stop 'Ex Parte Reexam' at the Central Reexamination Unit; hand-carried or delivery-service submissions should be taken to the Customer Service Window and also marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place Mail Stop information prominently on the first page of each filing. Requests for ex parte reexamination may not be sent by facsimile; corrected/completed requests (which replace the original) also cannot be faxed. Subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence may be faxed to Central Reexamination Unit at the provided fax number. Since July 9, 2007, the Office accepts requests and permitted 'follow-on' papers via EFS-Web per the Legal Framework for EFS-Web (link provided in MPEP). Identify the proceeding by patent number, request control number, art unit, and examiner in letters after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing/express mail procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) and the 'Express Mail' procedures (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file any paper in an ex parte reexamination proceeding except for a request for reexamination and a corrected/replacement request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures may be used for filing patent owner statements under 37 CFR 1.530 and requester replies under 37 CFR 1.535, among other papers. See MPEP §§ 512 and 513 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing papers directed to merits prior to decision on request
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination, no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than (A) citations of patents or printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 or 1.555, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP § 2282, should be filed with the Office prior to the date of the decision on the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any improper merit-directed papers filed before the decision will be returned to sender or expunged; if entered prior to discovery they will be expunged and a record of the notification will be placed in the patent file. Such papers may be filed/accepted later in proceedings if appropriate. See Patlex Corp. v. Mossinghoff and In re Knight for related precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date assignment, notices of failure to comply, and limited cure opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not include the required fee or meet all requirements, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity (generally 30 days) to complete the request. Failure to comply may result in the request not being granted a filing date and placement as a citation (37 CFR 1.510(c)). The filing date is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial clerical screening is performed by the CRU. PTOL-2077 is used for 'Notice of Failure to Comply' and PTOL-2057 for fee deficiencies. Absent extraordinary circumstances, requester ordinarily receives only one opportunity to correct defects; responses that introduce new defects can prevent assignment of a filing date. If non-compliance is discovered after a filing date is assigned, OPLA may issue a Decision Vacating Filing Date and provide an opportunity to correct; failure to remedy may lead to vacating the proceeding. Procedures describe which office personnel handle memos/decisions and the chain of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of filed requests in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of filing of all complete ex parte reexamination requests will be published in the Official Gazette approximately 4–5 weeks after filing. Both reexamination requests and Director-initiated orders to reexamine will be announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU preprocessing staff completes forms supplying information needed for printing the notice; notices include the requester name and other items required by 37 CFR 1.11(c). Publication in the Official Gazette provides public announcement of filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice when patent owner cannot be reached
rubrics_metrics.description: If all efforts to correspond with the patent owner fail because no current address is available, the publication in the Official Gazette of the notice of the filing of a request for reexamination or ordering of reexamination will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may continue without actual notice to the patent owner where actual delivery is impossible; Official Gazette publication serves as constructive notice in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of corrections to incomplete requests and marking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All processing of submissions to cure an incomplete request for ex parte reexamination is carried out in the preprocessing area of the CRU. Any such submission should be marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' so it may be promptly forwarded to reexamination preprocessing staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly marking submissions ensures timely routing. To obtain certified copies of reexamination files, a CD-ROM may be purchased from Document Services Division of OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public via Public PAIR, with the exception of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public PAIR shows the entire content of the reexamination file except non-patent literature (which is excluded). Instructions for accessing Public PAIR and ordering copies from Document Services (mailing address and email address) are provided. Copies may also be obtained from IFW via PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine if a reexamination request has been filed (PAIR/PALM procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for using the USPTO website Public PAIR and the USPTO intranet PALM to determine whether a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent number and to find the reexamination number and contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step navigation is provided for the public Internet and internal PALM access, including how ex parte and inter partes reexaminations are identified by unique series codes (e.g., '90' series for ex parte) and how to click through to the reexamination file contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and entity-size reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under reexamination there are fees for the request (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1)), for addition of claims (excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4)), for extensions of time, and for appeals and oral hearings. No fee is required for issuance of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small entity and micro entity reductions are available for certain fees (excess claim fees, appeal, appeal forwarding, oral hearing, and for the request and petition fees). When fees are required in a merged proceeding, only a single fee is needed. See relevant CFR sections and MPEP fee discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and format of amendments in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 (and manner of making amendments per 37 CFR 1.121). A proposed amendment is made by filing a paper directing that proposed specified changes be made to the patent specification, including the claims, or to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be submitted as accompaniment to a patent owner’s request (37 CFR 1.510(e)), as part of a patent owner statement under 1.530(b), or when permitted during prosecution under 1.550(a) or 1.937. Follow the procedural formatting and signature requirements in 1.121 and 1.530; see MPEP § 2250 and § 2234 for details.
